title: Mock 6 · Tough I: Numbers & Nuances
blurb: Exam-pressure set: multi-step numericals (net return, attribution, duration, Gordon), 'which is NOT' and two-statement regulatory traps.

questions.q: The nominal risk-free rate is 9.18% and expected inflation is 5%. Using the exact relationship, the real risk-free rate is closest to:
questions.explanation: (1 + real) = 1.0918 / 1.05 = 1.0398, so real ≈ 3.98%. Simple subtraction (4.18%) is only an approximation.
hints: Wrong: adds the two rates with a cross term.

questions.q: Statement I: Required rate of return is the minimum return an investor expects and is not a guaranteed return. Statement II: Required rate of return is the same as the realised return. Which is correct?
questions.explanation: The workbook states the required return is the minimum return investors expect; it is not guaranteed and differs from expected and realised returns.
hints: Wrong: required return differs from realised return.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about a bonus issue is NOT correct?
options: It is made without consideration from shareholders
It is made out of free reserves built from genuine profits
Once announced, it can be withdrawn by the board at any time before the record date
A company that has defaulted on interest on its debt securities cannot make a bonus issue
questions.explanation: A bonus issue once announced cannot be withdrawn. The other statements match the workbook.
hints: Correct: the false statement; bonus cannot be withdrawn once announced.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT included in the definition of 'securities' under Section 2(h) of the SCRA, 1956?
options: Units of a mutual fund scheme
Security receipts under the SARFAESI Act
questions.explanation: Securities include MF units, security receipts and government securities, but specifically exclude unit linked insurance policies.

questions.q: A company just paid a dividend (D0) of ₹4. Dividends are expected to grow at 8% forever and the required return is 12%. The intrinsic value per share is:
hints: Wrong: uses D0 instead of D1.

questions.q: Company X has a P/E of 18 while its industry and peers trade at 22. Other things equal, a relative valuation analyst would judge X to be:
options: Impossible to judge without its PEG
questions.explanation: The workbook's example: a target P/E of 18 versus 22 for the industry/market/comparables means the firm is judged undervalued.
hints: Wrong: it trades at a lower multiple.
Wrong: P/E comparison alone suffices for this judgement.

questions.q: Which combination of model and discount rate is correctly matched?
options: FCFF discounted at cost of equity gives equity value
FCFE discounted at WACC gives enterprise value
FCFF discounted at WACC gives enterprise value; equity = EV - Debt + Cash
Dividend discount model discounted at the coupon rate
questions.explanation: FCFF is discounted at WACC to obtain enterprise value; equity value = EV - Debt + Cash. FCFE is discounted at cost of equity.
hints: Wrong: FCFE pairs with cost of equity.
Wrong: DDM uses the required return on equity.

questions.q: A bond priced at ₹1,050 has a modified duration of 5. If yields FALL by 1%, the approximate new price is:
hints: Wrong: wrong sign; prices rise when yields fall.

questions.q: Four 10-year bonds experience the same rise in yield. Which will show the LARGEST percentage price fall?
questions.explanation: Price volatility is inversely related to coupon; with the same maturity, a zero coupon bond experiences the largest percentage price change.
hints: Correct: zero coupon is most volatile.

questions.q: Which statement about derivatives in a PMS is NOT correct?
options: PMs may use derivatives for hedging and portfolio rebalancing through recognised stock exchanges
The agreement must specify quantum of derivative exposure in absolute terms and as a percentage of other investments
A PM may leverage the client's portfolio up to twice its value for derivatives with written consent
PMs may participate in exchange traded commodity derivatives subject to regulatory stipulations and client consent
questions.explanation: Total derivative exposure should not exceed the client's portfolio value and PMs shall not leverage client portfolios for derivatives; consent does not change this.

questions.q: Which pairing of InvIT type and feature is INCORRECT?
options: Public InvIT: listed and open to retail investors
Private InvIT: unlisted and available to retail investors through SIPs
Full-fledged InvIT: invests in operational, revenue-generating assets
Developmental InvIT: invests in under-construction projects with higher risk
questions.explanation: Private InvITs are unlisted, privately placed and available only to institutional investors.
hints: Correct: incorrect pairing; private InvITs are for institutions only.

questions.q: A Fund of Funds that invests in multiple AIFs instead of holding assets directly is classified under:
questions.explanation: The workbook lists PE funds, debt funds and Fund of Funds as Category II examples.
hints: Wrong: Category I is VC, angel, social, infrastructure.
Wrong: social venture funds are Category I.

questions.q: Statement I: A non-discretionary portfolio manager provides investment management services, deciding what and when to buy. Statement II: In advisory services, the investor takes the decisions and also executes the transactions. Which is correct?
questions.explanation: A non-discretionary PM provides execution services, not investment management; decisions rest with the investor. In advisory, the investor decides and executes.

questions.q: The auditor's certificate on the PM's books, if so specified, must be submitted to SEBI within ______ of the close of the PM's accounting period, and the client receives a copy of the CA's certificate on the portfolio accounts audited ______.
options: One year; once every three years
questions.explanation: The certificate is submitted to SEBI within six months of the close of the accounting period; portfolio accounts are audited annually by an independent CA and a copy given to the client.
hints: Wrong: two months is for rectifying auditor deficiencies.

questions.q: A portfolio manager wishes to (i) impose a 2-year lock-in, (ii) charge 2.5% exit load in year 1, (iii) charge 1.5% exit load in year 3. Which of these are permissible?
questions.explanation: No lock-in can be imposed. Exit load caps are 3% (year 1), 2% (year 2), 1% (year 3), so 2.5% in year 1 is fine but 1.5% in year 3 exceeds the cap.

questions.q: A ₹1 crore PMS earns 18% gross in a year. Other expenses are 0.50% of the gross year-end value, fixed fee is 2% on the average of capital and gross value, and performance fee is 20% of profits above an 8% hurdle (no catch-up), computed after the fixed fee. There is no exit load. The net return is closest to:
hints: Wrong: stops after the fixed fee and skips expenses.
Wrong: applies performance fee on the full 18%.
Wrong: deducts an exit load that does not apply.

questions.q: Which item belongs to Part II (Dynamic Section) of the simplified PMS Disclosure Document?
options: Audit observations of the preceding 3 years
questions.explanation: Part II covers client representation, financial performance, PM performance, audit observations of the preceding 3 years and related party investments. The others are in Part I (static).

questions.q: Any deviation from the PM's written policy on order placement and allocation is permitted only:
options: With oral approval of the dealer
On account of exigency, with prior written approval of the Principal Officer and Compliance Officer and a detailed rationale
With approval of the client's distributor
After intimation to APMI within 30 days
questions.explanation: Deviations, if any, shall be on account of exigency only and require prior written approval of the Principal Officer and Compliance Officer with a detailed rationale.
hints: Wrong: written approval of senior officers is needed.
Wrong: distributors have no such role.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT among the actions SEBI can take against a defaulting portfolio manager under the Intermediaries Regulations, 2008, as listed in the workbook?
options: Compulsory transfer of all client portfolios to SEBI
Debarring the principal officer for a specified period
questions.explanation: Listed actions: suspension, cancellation, prohibition from new assignments, debarring principal officer, debarring a branch, warning. Transfer of portfolios to SEBI is not listed.

questions.q: On the workbook's sample questionnaire an investor answers: age below 30 (5), high growth (5), somewhat comfortable with short-term losses (4), 50-75% in equity (4), moderately stable income (4), horizon more than 10 years (5). The suggested strategy is:
questions.explanation: Total = 5 + 5 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 5 = 27, in the 25-30 Aggressive band, i.e., high equity exposure.

questions.q: Which of the following is a REGULATORY constraint rather than a personal preference?
options: An investor refusing to sell her employer's shares out of emotional attachment
A resident individual's overseas investment being limited to USD 2,50,000 per financial year under LRS
An investor needing funds for a child's wedding next year
questions.explanation: The LRS limit is a regulatory constraint. Emotional attachment and ethical exclusions are unique preferences; wedding funding is a liquidity need.

questions.q: Which statement about performance benchmarking of PMS is correct?
options: A PM may tag one investment approach to two strategies if the Board approves
Benchmarks are chosen freely by each PM without any list
After a change in strategy tagging, the old track record may be shown alongside the new benchmark
The Board of the PM is responsible for appropriate selection of strategy and benchmark for each IA
questions.explanation: The Board of the PM is responsible for selection. Each IA has exactly one strategy; benchmarks come from APMI's list (max 3 per strategy); past track record before a tagging change cannot be used.
hints: Wrong: old track record cannot be used.

questions.q: Which is listed in the workbook as a challenge or risk of factor-based investing?
questions.explanation: Challenges listed: factor cyclicality, data and implementation complexity, and overcrowding risks.
hints: Wrong: diversification is a listed benefit.

questions.q: Portfolio vs benchmark: Sector A Wp 50%, Rp 14%, Wb 40%, Rb 12%; Sector B Wp 30%, Rp 6%, Wb 40%, Rb 8%; Sector C Wp 20%, Rp 10%, Wb 20%, Rb 9%. The asset allocation effect is:
hints: Wrong: this is the selection effect.
Wrong: this is the total excess return.

questions.q: Using the same data (A: Wp 50%, Rp 14%, Wb 40%, Rb 12%; B: Wp 30%, Rp 6%, Wb 40%, Rb 8%; C: Wp 20%, Rp 10%, Wb 20%, Rb 9%), the security selection effect is:
hints: Wrong: this is the allocation (or interaction) effect.

questions.q: Fund X returned 18% with SD 20%; Fund Y returned 14% with SD 12%. Risk-free rate is 6%. Based on the Sharpe ratio:
questions.explanation: Sharpe X = (18 - 6) / 20 = 0.60; Sharpe Y = (14 - 6) / 12 = 0.67. Y gives more excess return per unit of total risk.
hints: Wrong: return / SD without subtracting Rf.

questions.q: An individual's F&O business turnover through PMS is ₹12 crore in a year, with a small profit. As per the workbook, a tax audit is:
options: Not required if over 95% of transactions are digital
Mandatory under Section 44AB(a) regardless of profit or loss
Required only if profit is below 6%
questions.explanation: For turnover above ₹10 crore, tax audit is mandatory under Section 44AB(a) regardless of profit or loss.
hints: Wrong: the 95% digital exemption applies to ₹2-10 crore.
Wrong: the 6% test applies up to ₹2 crore.

questions.q: Which statement on PMS taxation for a resident individual is NOT correct?
options: STCG on listed equity sold within 12 months is taxed at 20% with no exemption
Unabsorbed derivative business losses can be carried forward up to 8 assessment years
Debt STCG (24 months or less) is taxed at slab rates
Brokerage and performance fees can be deducted from capital gains if the investor shows them as expenses
questions.explanation: For individuals reporting capital gains, PMS fees including brokerage, GST and performance fees are not deductible. The other statements are correct.

questions.q: Under the insider trading code of conduct, a 'material financial relationship' exists when a person has received from the designated person, during the immediately preceding twelve months, a payment such as a loan or gift equivalent to at least:
options: 25% of the designated person's annual income
10% of the designated person's annual income
50% of the designated person's net worth
questions.explanation: Material financial relationship = recipient of payment (loan, gift) during the preceding 12 months equivalent to at least 25% of the designated person's annual income, excluding arm's length transactions.
hints: Wrong: based on annual income, not net worth.
Wrong: ₹10 lakh is the PMLA cash threshold.

questions.q: A portfolio manager offers non-discretionary services to an ordinary (non-accredited) client with AUM of ₹2 crore. The maximum that may be invested in unlisted securities for this client is:
questions.explanation: Non-discretionary or advisory PMs may invest up to 25% of AUM in unlisted securities: 25% x ₹2 crore = ₹50 lakh. Up to 100% is allowed only for large value accredited investors.
hints: Wrong: 100% only for large value accredited investors.
